subject: APAC region throttling impact — evidence request and remediation plan
messages:
From: Megan Liu <megan@kilncommerce.com>
To: mateo@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 07:16:00 -0700
Subject: APAC: We saw sustained 503s / token throttling 06/20 — confirmation needed

Hi Mateo,

We observed a 40–60 minute window of elevated 503s and increased tail latency between ~01:20–02:05 UTC on 2027-06-20 that impacted our checkout flow in APAC (SG). We have transaction traces and user impact counts if helpful.

Before we open a formal claim, can you confirm whether Redwood observed any routing or capacity-related throttling in the APAC pool during that window and whether this would qualify under the standard uptime SLO for potential credit? Kiln Commerce is running a mission-critical checkout and would like an initial read so we can escalate internally.

Attached: small trace sample (trace_ids_utc_20270620.txt) and a quick error-rate chart exported from our side.

Thanks — appreciate a quick read.

Megan Liu

Megan — thanks for flagging this and for sending the trace ids. Sorry this hit your checkout.

Quick update: I’ve opened an internal verification ticket and looped Priya (Customer Success) and Marcus (SRE) to pull the raw service side logs and routing decisions for the APAC pool for the window you reported. We’ll validate whether the events align with an SLA-eligible availability impact vs transient client-side errors.

Next steps from Redwood side (ETA in this thread):
- Marcus will pull the raw request logs + kernel-level timeouts and share a sanitized tarball.
- We’ll correlate your trace IDs against request_ids in our logs and provide a list of matching request_ids and timestamps.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: mateo@redwood.com, priya@redwood.com
Cc: hschmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC: We saw sustained 503s / token throttling 06/20 — confirmation needed

Mateo / Priya — I pulled the APAC pool logs and a short metrics dump for 2027-06-20 00:30–03:00 UTC. Preliminary findings:

- We saw a surge in queue depth on node set apac-prod-14 between 01:18–01:54 UTC with a matched spike in request timeouts at the transport layer.
- There were two autoscaler events in the period, but the scale-up window was ~45s and did not fully recover queue depth in a few hot buckets.
- No configuration changes or deploys were recorded in the window.
- Initial correlation against the trace IDs Megan provided found 37 matching request_ids; I’ll upload the sanitized mapping.

Artifacts attached: raw_logs_apac_20270620.tar.gz (sanitized), trace_ids_utc_20270620.txt (mapping), service-metrics-20270620.csv (aggregated counters). I removed IPs and any customer PII.

Question for the SLA team: given the sustained queueing and partial autoscale slow path, should this be treated as an availability incident (SLA credit eligible) vs transient throttling? My leaning is availability impact because it increased error rate and we failed to meet the latency SLO for % p99 tokens across the pool for >30m.

Cc’ing Hannah to weigh in on credit eligibility and postmortem scope.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

--
Attachment: raw_logs_apac_20270620.tar.gz (archive)
Attachment: trace_ids_utc_20270620.txt (text)
Attachment: service-metrics-20270620.csv (csv)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hschmitt@redwood.com>
To: Megan Liu <megan@kilncommerce.com>, mateo@redwood.com
Cc: priya@redwood.com, marcus@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: APAC: We saw sustained 503s / token throttling 06/20 — confirmation needed

Hi Megan — thanks for your patience and for the artifacts.

Summary/decision: based on the logs Marcus provided and the matched request_ids, Redwood confirms there was a sustained availability impact in the APAC inference pool between 2027-06-20T01:18:00Z and 2027-06-20T01:54:00Z that materially increased 5xxs and p99 latency for affected customers in the region. Per section 3.2 of your contract and our SLO language, that window appears eligible for a credit evaluation.

What we will deliver in the next 72 hours:
- A postmortem draft focused on root cause (autoscaler slow path + hot-bucket queueing) and action items to prevent recurrence.
- A proposed credit calculation using the contract formula (downtime minutes and affected capacity fraction) and an amortized credit amount; we’ll include a worked example for Kiln Commerce.
- A sanitized evidence bundle (logs + mapping + metrics) for your audit.

Can you confirm whether Kiln would prefer the credit applied to your next invoice or an API usage rebate for the current billing period? Also confirm if you want Redwood to provide a short remediation playbook that your ops team can run during a future spike (warmup, request retry guidance, and optional routing hints).

We’ll mark this P0 and share the postmortem and credit calc by EOD Thu, 2027-06-24.

Thanks — Hannah Schmitt
Director, Customer Reliability
